html:
A Greek mathematician and architect from Tralles in Asia Minor, who designed Hagia Sophia in Constantinople with Isidore of Miletus. He came from a learned family; his brothers included a doctor and a lawyer.

After the Nika riots burned the old church in 532, Justinian gave the two men the job of building a new one, and it was finished in less than six years. Its huge dome on four arches was bolder than anything built before, and it rested on their grasp of geometry rather than on long building practice.

Anthemius also wrote on geometry, including a work on burning mirrors that focus sunlight, and on conic sections. A later writer tells how he annoyed a neighbour by faking an earthquake with steam. He died, perhaps around 534, before the earthquake of 557 cracked his dome, which fell the next year and was rebuilt higher by Isidore's nephew.
